A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Task Vector Bases research, despite v4's new title and substantial redesign. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original clustering, model-merging, MNIST unlearning, and held-out-task experiments, including Tables 4–8 and the 70-task language study.

after.justification: v4 reports original autoencoder-basis addition, negation, and continual-learning experiments, including generative-language results in Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: v2's spectral clustering, eigengap selection, and cluster-wise merging are replaced by a softmax-encoder/linear-decoder reconstruction method optimized through a Gram matrix. v4 also introduces encoder-weighted merging losses, reconstructed-vector negation, and fixed-budget online recompression; its L&S adaptation replaces the earlier Mask Sharing/Stitch Twice procedures (Section 3.2).

E1.justification: The eight vision and twelve language datasets are retained, but v4 adds 14-/20-task vision collections and generative-language evaluation covering instruction following, mathematics, multilingual tasks, coding, and safety. The 70-task classification study disappears, and GTSRB/DTD held-out transfer is replaced by six other vision targets under few-shot adaptation (Appendix F).

E2.justification: v4 adds PCA, RandSelect, positive-weighted PCA, and RandProj compression comparisons, plus MagMax and OPCM continual baselines. Fisher, RegMean, AdaMerging, and Consensus rows from v2's twelve-task comparison (Table 15) disappear from v4's corresponding comparison; some remain only as explanatory method examples.

E3.justification: v4 uses matched 50%-vision/25%-language basis budgets across compression methods, stratified validation subsampling proportional to M/T, two-/sixteen-shot aTLAS controls, and full sequential buffer evaluation. It also reports validation-grid tuning for vision TIES over 0–1 in 0.05 increments, whereas v2 Appendix C.5 fixes its coefficient at 0.4. These are substantive reported protocol changes.

E4.justification: v4 replaces exhaustive cluster-partition, early-checkpoint clustering, and adversarial-prompt analyses with studies of PCA failure, autoencoder temperature/reconstruction, subsampling, loss weighting, and basis-budget tradeoffs (Tables 9–12 and Figures 1–4, 8). The earlier norm, similarity, smoothness, and empirical loss-gap checks are retained in Appendix D, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports mean and standard deviation across five task orders (Table 16) and averages runtime across three runs (Table 10). v2 Figure 8 instead mentions five random partitions without uncertainty bars. This reporting expansion is limited to particular studies and does not establish increased runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: The clustering-result tables and 70-task curve are replaced by extensive AE results, including new generative and continual evaluations. On the retained twelve-task benchmark, reported full-vector TA changes from 67.5 in v2 Table 15 to 62.6 in v4 Table 2, while L&S remains 75.9. Changed procedures prevent interpreting the revision as a matched performance gain; the earlier loss-gap and checkpoint-mixing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The original task-addition, negation, and OOD bounds and proofs remain in v4 Appendix B. v4 adds the Gram reformulation, a softmax spectral-optimality theorem, and guarantees specifically for compressed bases, including an OOD coverage/alignment condition and reconstruction-error penalties for negation (Theorems 3.4–3.7).

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes explaining ordinary task arithmetic and saving memory through clustered bases. v4 makes unified task-vector compression the central contribution, claims reductions in both storage and composition computation, and adds principled autoencoder construction and compressed-basis guarantees. These change the substantive scope of the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: The basis-design explanation shifts from near-orthogonal clusters and disjoint task groups to convex-cone alignment and reconstruction quality. v4 adds substantive discussions of PCA's incompatibilities, forgetting-versus-retention tradeoffs, and why near-optimal reconstruction can still require temperature tuning for good addition (Sections 3.1, 4.2, and Appendix E.1).

D1.justification: v4 Appendices E–F specify autoencoder optimization defaults, Gram computation, merging grids, mask-training settings, online coefficients, and runtime measurements. Conversely, v2's detailed initial RoBERTa fine-tuning recipe and extensive prompt, label-mapping, and dataset-access catalog are removed. The code-access URL is retained.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from task-arithmetic theory and task grouping toward compression, quantization, low-rank merging, and matrix factorization. v4 adds substantive comparisons with TSV/subspace methods, nonnegative PCA/NMF, and dictionary learning, alongside new PCA/autoencoder foundations (Section 5 and Appendix A.3–A.4), while removing v2's extended NTK and task-grouping discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with a new title. Experiments are reorganized by arithmetic application instead of primarily by vision/language domain; related work moves after experiments, and detailed theoretical assumptions and empirical theory checks move into appendices.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes single-column, and the visual presentation is extensively rebuilt around compression tables, PCA geometry, radar charts, runtime plots, and encoder heatmaps. Earlier clustering/storage illustrations and partition tables disappear. Retained v2 Figures 3/6 and 4/5 are paired and relocated as v4 Figures 5 and 6.

improvement.justification: v2 motivates clustered bases mainly through bounds for ordinary task vectors and small vision case studies. v4 directly analyzes compressed representations and adds compression baselines, subsampling controls, runtime evidence, and repeated-order continual evaluation. This substantially strengthens the connection between the proposed framework and its supporting evidence. Removing the 70-task stress test weakens that aspect of scalability validation, and performance advantages are not uniform, but the overall methodological and evidential gains are substantial.
